This report uses the focal-variable mappings listed below. It selects the baseline sample-description variables, baseline focal items, and
EMA focal items; merges baseline information onto prompt-level EMA rows; and
saves the single analysis-entry RDA file used by later stages.

No scale total, scale mean, reverse-scored item, day-level aggregation, or other
composite is created here. Item descriptives are calculated separately at the
baseline participant level and EMA prompt level.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  collapse = FALSE,
  comment = NA
)

required_packages <- c("dplyr", "knitr", "psych", "rmarkdown", "tidyr")
package_available <- vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (!all(package_available)) {
  stop("Missing required R packages: ", paste(names(package_available)[!package_available], collapse = ", "))
}

locate_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  current <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  if (!dir.exists(current)) current <- dirname(current)
  repeat {
    if (all(dir.exists(file.path(current, c(
      "Step_1_Descriptive_and_Reliability", "Step_2_Measurement_Models"
    ))))) return(current)
    parent <- dirname(current)
    if (identical(parent, current)) break
    current <- parent
  }
  stop("Could not locate the project from its public Step directories")
}

input_path <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
project_root <- locate_project_root(if (is.null(input_path)) getwd() else input_path)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

input_file <- file.path(project_root, "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis", "dat_clean_components.rda")
output_file <- file.path(project_root, "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis", "dat_focal_analysis.rda")

if (!file.exists(input_file)) stop("Missing S1.1 input RDA: ", input_file)
```

# Variable specification

The study's original variable specification defines four EMA item groups and
four baseline item groups. Their full mappings are encoded here; the original
Word reference is not required to run the analysis.

```{r variable-specification}
sample_description_vars <- c(
  "AgeInYears",
  "Gender",
  "Grade",
  "FamilyResidence",
  "ParentsMaritalStatus",
  "ParentsHighestEdu",
  "TotalFamilyIncome",
  "SiblingStructure"
)

baseline_item_map <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(variable = paste0("V_BSMAS_", 1:18), construct = "Trait PSMU (BSMAS)", expected_min = 1, expected_max = 5, reverse_keyed = FALSE),
  data.frame(variable = paste0("K_CESD_", 1:7), construct = "Depression (CES-D selected items)", expected_min = 1, expected_max = 4, reverse_keyed = FALSE),
  # The Word document states 0-3, whereas the clean RDA is coded 1-4.
  data.frame(variable = paste0("L_DASS_", 1:7), construct = "Anxiety (DASS selected items)", expected_min = 0, expected_max = 3, reverse_keyed = FALSE),
  data.frame(
    variable = paste0("M_PSS_", 1:10),
    construct = "Perceived stress (PSS-10)",
    expected_min = 1,
    expected_max = 5,
    reverse_keyed = 1:10 %in% c(4, 5, 7, 8)
  )
)

ema_item_map <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  # The Word document states 1-300, whereas the clean RDA includes zero.
  data.frame(variable = paste0("mu_time", 1:3), construct = "Social media use time", expected_min = 1, expected_max = 300, reverse_keyed = FALSE),
  data.frame(variable = paste0("mu_frequency", 1:3), construct = "Social media use frequency", expected_min = 1, expected_max = 4, reverse_keyed = FALSE),
  data.frame(variable = paste0("PMU", 1:6), construct = "Momentary problematic social media use", expected_min = 1, expected_max = 5, reverse_keyed = FALSE),
  # The Word document does not state response anchors for momentary DASS items.
  data.frame(variable = paste0("DASS", 1:6), construct = "Momentary depression/anxiety/stress", expected_min = NA_real_, expected_max = NA_real_, reverse_keyed = FALSE)
)

baseline_focal_vars <- baseline_item_map$variable
ema_focal_vars <- ema_item_map$variable

baseline_item_map |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Variable specification",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
ema_item_map |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Variable specification (2)",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

# Load and validate S1.1 data

```{r load-and-validate}
input_environment <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
loaded_objects <- load(input_file, envir = input_environment)
required_objects <- c("dat_baseline", "dat_ema")
if (!all(required_objects %in% loaded_objects)) {
  stop("Input RDA is missing objects: ", paste(setdiff(required_objects, loaded_objects), collapse = ", "))
}
dat_baseline <- input_environment[["dat_baseline"]]
dat_ema <- input_environment[["dat_ema"]]

required_baseline_vars <- c("Name_ID", sample_description_vars, baseline_focal_vars)
required_ema_vars <- c("Data_ID", "Name_ID", "Day", "Time", ema_focal_vars)

missing_baseline_vars <- setdiff(required_baseline_vars, names(dat_baseline))
missing_ema_vars <- setdiff(required_ema_vars, names(dat_ema))
if (length(missing_baseline_vars)) {
  stop("Missing baseline variables: ", paste(missing_baseline_vars, collapse = ", "))
}
if (length(missing_ema_vars)) {
  stop("Missing EMA variables: ", paste(missing_ema_vars, collapse = ", "))
}

baseline_duplicate_ids <- dat_baseline |>
  dplyr::count(Name_ID, name = "n") |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 1L)

ema_duplicate_prompt_keys <- dat_ema |>
  dplyr::count(Name_ID, Day, Time, name = "n") |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 1L)

stopifnot(
  nrow(baseline_duplicate_ids) == 0L,
  nrow(ema_duplicate_prompt_keys) == 0L,
  !anyNA(dat_baseline$Name_ID),
  !anyNA(dat_ema[c("Name_ID", "Day", "Time")])
)

data.frame(
  source = c("Baseline", "EMA"),
  rows = c(nrow(dat_baseline), nrow(dat_ema)),
  participants = c(dplyr::n_distinct(dat_baseline$Name_ID), dplyr::n_distinct(dat_ema$Name_ID)),
  duplicate_key_groups = c(nrow(baseline_duplicate_ids), nrow(ema_duplicate_prompt_keys))
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Load and validate",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

# Helper functions

```{r helpers}
variable_label <- function(x) {
  label <- attr(x, "label", exact = TRUE)
  if (is.null(label)) NA_character_ else as.character(label)
}

item_descriptives <- function(data, item_map) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(item_map)), function(i) {
    variable <- item_map$variable[[i]]
    x <- data[[variable]]
    observed <- x[!is.na(x)]
    description <- if (length(observed) >= 3L) psych::describe(observed, fast = FALSE) else NULL
    data.frame(
      construct = item_map$construct[[i]],
      variable = variable,
      item_label = variable_label(x),
      n_total = length(x),
      n_valid = length(observed),
      n_missing = sum(is.na(x)),
      missing_percent = 100 * mean(is.na(x)),
      mean = if (length(observed)) mean(observed) else NA_real_,
      sd = if (length(observed) > 1L) stats::sd(observed) else NA_real_,
      median = if (length(observed)) stats::median(observed) else NA_real_,
      minimum = if (length(observed)) min(observed) else NA_real_,
      maximum = if (length(observed)) max(observed) else NA_real_,
      skewness = if (is.null(description)) NA_real_ else description$skew,
      kurtosis = if (is.null(description)) NA_real_ else description$kurtosis,
      reverse_keyed = item_map$reverse_keyed[[i]],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

range_audit <- function(descriptives, item_map) {
  descriptives |>
    dplyr::select(variable, observed_min = minimum, observed_max = maximum) |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      item_map |>
        dplyr::select(variable, expected_min, expected_max),
      by = "variable"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      documented_range_available = !is.na(expected_min) & !is.na(expected_max),
      within_documented_range = dplyr::if_else(
        documented_range_available,
        observed_min >= expected_min & observed_max <= expected_max,
        NA
      ),
      note = dplyr::case_when(
        grepl("^L_DASS_", variable) & !within_documented_range ~ "Word document: 0-3; clean RDA: 1-4. Original coding retained.",
        grepl("^mu_time", variable) & !within_documented_range ~ "Word document: 1-300; clean RDA includes 0. Original coding retained.",
        !documented_range_available ~ "Response range not stated in the focal-variable Word document.",
        within_documented_range ~ "Observed values fall within the documented range.",
        TRUE ~ "Observed values fall outside the documented range; inspect before modeling."
      )
    )
}

categorical_descriptives <- function(data, variables) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(variables, function(variable) {
    values <- data[[variable]]
    tab <- table(values, useNA = "ifany")
    data.frame(
      variable = variable,
      category = names(tab),
      n = as.integer(tab),
      percent_of_sample = 100 * as.integer(tab) / length(values),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}
```

# Baseline section

Baseline descriptives are computed once per participant from `dat_baseline`,
before baseline variables are repeated across EMA prompts in the merged file.

## Sample description

```{r baseline-sample-description}
baseline_sample <- dat_baseline |>
  dplyr::select(Name_ID, dplyr::all_of(sample_description_vars))

baseline_sample |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    participants = dplyr::n_distinct(Name_ID),
    age_n = sum(!is.na(AgeInYears)),
    age_missing = sum(is.na(AgeInYears)),
    age_mean = mean(AgeInYears, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_sd = stats::sd(AgeInYears, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_median = stats::median(AgeInYears, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_minimum = min(AgeInYears, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_maximum = max(AgeInYears, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline sample description",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )

baseline_categorical_descriptives <- categorical_descriptives(
  baseline_sample,
  setdiff(sample_description_vars, "AgeInYears")
)
baseline_categorical_descriptives |>
  dplyr::mutate(percent_of_sample = round(percent_of_sample, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline sample description (2)",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Baseline focal-item descriptives

No baseline scale total, mean, or reverse-scored value is computed. The
`reverse_keyed` column records the Word document's PSS key for later scoring
only.

```{r baseline-item-descriptives}
baseline_item_descriptives <- item_descriptives(dat_baseline, baseline_item_map)

baseline_item_descriptives |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline item descriptives",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed item-description-table"'
  )
```

## Baseline range audit

```{r baseline-range-audit}

baseline_range_audit |>

```

# EMA section

EMA descriptives are computed at the prompt level. No prompt-to-day aggregation
or scale construction is performed.

## EMA observation structure

```{r ema-observation-structure}
dat_ema |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    participants = dplyr::n_distinct(Name_ID),
    person_days = dplyr::n_distinct(paste(Name_ID, Day)),
    prompts = dplyr::n(),
    minimum_day = min(Day, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum_day = max(Day, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Ema observation structure",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )

dat_ema |>
  dplyr::count(Time, name = "scheduled_rows") |>
  dplyr::arrange(Time) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Ema observation structure (2)",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

# Merge and save the single analysis-entry RDA

The merged data remain at EMA prompt level. Baseline fields are attached by the
unique participant key `Name_ID` using an explicitly validated many-to-one join.

```{r merge-and-save}
dat_baseline_focal <- dat_baseline |>
  dplyr::select(
    Name_ID,
    dplyr::all_of(sample_description_vars),
    dplyr::all_of(baseline_focal_vars)
  )

dat_ema_focal <- dat_ema |>
  dplyr::select(
    Data_ID,
    Name_ID,
    Day,
    Time,
    dplyr::all_of(ema_focal_vars)
  )

baseline_ids_missing_from_ema <- setdiff(dat_baseline_focal$Name_ID, dat_ema_focal$Name_ID)
ema_ids_missing_from_baseline <- setdiff(dat_ema_focal$Name_ID, dat_baseline_focal$Name_ID)

if (length(ema_ids_missing_from_baseline)) {
  stop("EMA participants missing from baseline: ", length(ema_ids_missing_from_baseline))
}

dat_focal_analysis <- dat_ema_focal |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dat_baseline_focal,
    by = "Name_ID",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    Data_ID,
    Name_ID,
    Day,
    Time,
    dplyr::all_of(sample_description_vars),
    dplyr::all_of(baseline_focal_vars),
    dplyr::all_of(ema_focal_vars)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID, Day, Time)

expected_columns <- c(
  "Data_ID", "Name_ID", "Day", "Time",
  sample_description_vars,
  baseline_focal_vars,
  ema_focal_vars
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(dat_focal_analysis) == nrow(dat_ema_focal),
  identical(names(dat_focal_analysis), expected_columns),
  dplyr::n_distinct(dat_focal_analysis$Name_ID) == dplyr::n_distinct(dat_ema_focal$Name_ID),
  nrow(dat_focal_analysis) == dplyr::n_distinct(paste(dat_focal_analysis$Name_ID, dat_focal_analysis$Day, dat_focal_analysis$Time)),
  !anyNA(dat_focal_analysis[c("Name_ID", "Day", "Time")])
)

if (isTRUE(params$write_artifacts)) {
  save(dat_focal_analysis, file = output_file, compress = "xz")
}

data.frame(
  output_file = "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis/dat_focal_analysis.rda",
  object = "dat_focal_analysis",
  rows = nrow(dat_focal_analysis),
  columns = ncol(dat_focal_analysis),
  participants = dplyr::n_distinct(dat_focal_analysis$Name_ID),
  bytes = file.info(output_file)$size,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Merge and save",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )

id_audit <- list(
  baseline_ids_missing_from_ema = baseline_ids_missing_from_ema,
  ema_ids_missing_from_baseline = ema_ids_missing_from_baseline
)

data.frame(
  comparison = names(id_audit),
  unmatched_count = lengths(id_audit),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Merge and save (2)",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```
